title: tvt: jar file export error message constructed incorrectly for nl (jarfileexportoperation.exportedwithcompile)
description: the message displayed when errors were found while exporting a class that doesn't compile to a jar file are incorrect. the spanish text: exportado con compilación errores: ... corresponds to the following properties file: eclipse\\plugins\\org.eclipse.jdt.ui\\jdt_jar\\org\\eclipse\\jdt\\internal\\ui\\jarpackag er\\jarpackagermessages.properties jarfileexportoperation.exportedwithcompile=exportado con compilaci¢n jarfileexportoperation.notexportedduetocompile=no exportado debido a la compilaci¢n jarfileexportoperation.errors=\\ errores: {0} jarfileexportoperation.warnings=\\ avisos: {0} the english file is as following: jarfileexportoperation.exportedwithcompile=exported with compile jarfileexportoperation.notexportedduetocompile=not exported due to compile jarfileexportoperation.errors=\\ errors: {0} jarfileexportoperation.warnings=\\ warnings: {0} these 4 strings combine to form the following sentences: exported wth compile errors: {0} exported with compile warnings: {0} not exported due to compile errors: {0} not exporte due to compile warnings: {0} this string structure makes it impossible to obtain a good translation in spanish because the translation of the word compile must be placed at the very end of the sentence. i can make a workaround to this problem, but the strings should be rewritten, either as the actual 4 sentences that appear or as only two sentences replacing errors and warnings with a variable, i.e.: exported with compile {1}: {0} not exported due to compile {1}: {0} in general, it is poor nl enablement practice to \\"construct\\" sentences. if you must use such techniques, allow for substitution as described above.

title: dcr: debugger should catch uncaught exception by default
description: from an eclipse corner post: one of the things i always do when i am debugging in eclipse (i did this in vame as well) is go to the debugger's \\"breakpoints\\" view, click on the view's \\"add java exception breakpoint\\" button, type \\"throwable\\" in the text field, and make sure only \\"uncaught\\" is checked. then click ok. what this does is tell the debugger to catch any uncaught throwables for me. i find this *much* handier than ending up with a stack trace in the console. if an unexpected exception happens, i am still in the debugger, and i can select frames in the stack trace and go right to the current line in the frame... i can also still see the values of variables, because my vm has not halted yet. i never delete this breakpoint. every time i run a java program under the debugger the \\"uncaught throwable\\" breakpoint is always there in the background... protecting me from myself . the response to this post was as follows: \\"that sounds like a great technique; thanks! (why isn't that the default behavior? :-) \\" please consider making this the default behavior.

title: associating classpath variables to ant properties
description: original message on the newsgroup: i'm using an ant script to try to run javacc (sort of a lex/yacc for java). javacc is itself written in java, so you run it by doing something like: java -classpath \\"blahblahblah\\" com.sun.labs.javacc.main parser.jj my ant script runs fine with hard-coded paths for the path to the javacc.zip file and the jvm, but that's not good, because different machines have these things installed in different places. after a bit of poking around into the eclipse's classpath mechanism, i thought that it might serve to define the locations of global (not project-specific) resources. so, i created a \\"javacc\\" classpath variable to point at the folder where javacc is installed. i noticed while doing this that there was classpath variable \\"eclipse_home\\", which i thought could give me access to java.exe. i then wrote an ant script like this: this doesn't work, on two counts: - ${eclipse_home} doesn't seem to get expanded as i would think, so ant can't find java.exe. - ${javacc} doesn't get expanded the way i thought it would, so that even if i use a hard-coded path rather ${eclipse_home}, i get a \\"class not found\\" error for com.sun.labs.javacc.main. am i mistaken in thinking that eclipse classpath variables can be used for this purpose? if so, what can i use to get what i'm after? [if this were a makefile, i'd use environment variables, but i've gotten the impression that there's no way to get at environment variables from java (and presumably, from within ant).] in case it matters, i'm running eclipse 1.0 r0.137 on windows nt, but of course i'd like a portable solution (e.g. that works under linux). -- robert m. fuhrer, phd dev_0262 ibm t.j. watson research center pgp public key available on request

title: java editor and special case display of bidi comments/strings
description: in the following examples, hebrew letters are represented by upper case latin letters. open a java editor window, insert a new line and type: string mystring = \\"abc\\" + \\"def\\"; // this is a comment the expected display should be: string mystring = \\"cba\\" + \\"fed\\"; // tnemmoc a si siht the actual display is: string mystring = \\"tnemmoc a si siht // ;\\"fed\\" + \\"cba currently in the java editor, the call that handled this special case is commented out (setbidicoloring). new api exists for handling this case. a new listener, bidisegmentlistener, has been created which one can use to specify how a line should be rendered for bidi purposes. see bidisegmentevent and bidisegmentlistener for more information. you essentially answer the distinct segments for a line. each segment is then reordered separately. for purposes of the java editor, you need only segment a line based on string literals. while you can segment the line based on each java syntactic element, this will be much more inefficient because it will be calling the bidi reordering platform function unnecessarily (as happening now for the setbidicoloring behavior). we hacked the java editor to just segment lines based on string literals and it all worked fine.

title: project dependencies not updated when .classpath file is read-only[pr 1glevo4]
description: pr 1glevo4 case 1: 1) create two java projects project1 and project2 2) make the .classpath file for project1 read-only (rmb on .classpath file, choose properties, check read only) 3) update project1's java build path to include project2 (rmb on project1, choose properties, choose java build path, choose projects tab) 4) to the user it looks like this has occurred without problem (it's still in project1's java build path, and calls to the javamodel return the correct information) but since the .classpath file is read-only, this change has never occured). at this point we believe the user should have been told that the file could not be updated. 5) bring down the workbench and bring it back up, and it is no longer in project1's java build path. case 2: here is another scenario (which i have not verified, but it seems right): the programmer creates a new project called abc and does not chose to use the default directory. instead, he points to the directory in clearcase containing the existing project files. as part of the java project create, it creates a new .classpath file. it does not look to see if there is an existing .classpath file (where in this case there is and its read-only). because we are talking about a clearcase controlled directory, the project create process results in a private read-write copy of the .classpath file being created. so now the newly created project sees a virgin .classpath file, not the one that was already there. proposed solution: if an existing .classpath file is detected, ask if it should be used before creating a new one. this is from a critical customer

title: toggling between problems with hotkey doesn't update status line
description: build 20020205 if you have a java class with multiple build problems, you can use ctrl+e and ctrl+shift+e to toggle between the problems. unfortunately using the hotkeys does not update the error message in the status line, so it is not possible to figure out what the error message is. if you use the actions in the edit menu, the status line is correctly updated. this is an accessibility problem for mouseless users that don't want to use the task list.

title: debug/run history menu items should be disabled if no history yet
description: start up a fresh install of the workbench, or at least one in which neither run nor debug has been used. (purge the metadata perhaps) select the debug menu item from the menu bar. notice that the debug history and run history menu items are visible, enabled, and have the little arrow indicating they have a submenu. however, if you hover over these items, no submenu pops up. this behaviour is misleading since obviously you cannot access any debug or run history. if either the debug or run history is empty, the corresponding menu item should either not appear, or be disabled.

title: debugger - tooltip in source view displays wrong value when variables have same name [editor]
description: how to reproduce: .use the code below .set a breakpoint at 'line 3' .when the debugger reaches this breakpoint, move the mouse on top of the word 'value' in line 1 inside the debug source view. the tooltip displays 7. this is the value of the local variable in the current frame, not the value of the field 'this.value' as expected. .move the mouse on top of 'this.value' at line 3. again, 7 and not 5 is displayed by the tooltip. .you can also select 'value' at line 1, right click and select 'display'. it shows 7 instead of 5. the information in the 'variables' view is correct. public class foo { int value = 5; // line 1 public void test() { int value = 7; // line 2 system.out.println(\\"value \\"+value+ \\", \\"+ this.value); // line 3 } public static void main(string args[]) { foo foo = new foo(); foo.test(); } }

title: format does not handle synchronized keyword correctly
description: when coding java: if i type in a code block such as the following we have a one line if statement that does not need brackets around it. if (bool) synchronized (this) { // dosomething } if right click and select format the format incorrectly formats this code to: if (bool) synchronized (this) { // dosomething } it correctly associates the opening brace with synchronized, but incorrectly associates the closing brace with the if statement. this is pretty annoying.

title: adding extra properties to a java file
description: i would like to be able to add extra properties to a java file - like parameters to an applet (like in vaj).

title: jdtcompileradapter ignores -nowarn and deprecation off.
description: in the source file jdtcompileradapter after checking all the options from ant it then specifically adds in all the warn options. \\"-warn:contructorname,packagedefaultmethod,maskedcatchblocks,deprecation\\". if a nowarn option is passed in from ant javac element these should not be turned on. -nowarn in the eclipse compiler states it is equivalent to -warn:non. this would make it possible to build with ant without warnings. i know about deprecation already in our source code. thanks, jcl.

title: structured selection key shortcuts should use shift key
description: currently, structured selection shortcuts are defined as alt- . this is different then the other range selection shortcuts that use the shift key. structured selection shortcuts can be changed to use alt-shift- , that would make them fit better with the rest of the text selection shortcuts. also, alt- shortcuts are frequently used for going back and forward in browsers and applications presenting similar functionality. these shortcuts would clash with similar functionality plugins may present in eclipse (which my nox browser plugin at http://sourceforge.net/projects/nox does).

title: compare preference text entry not accessible
description: the text font label is not accessible as it is a label with no associated control and will not be read by jaws . it should be in a group labelled text font with the font value and the change button in it.

title: content outline selection is slow
description: build 20020214 selection speed in the java content outline is slow, especially when using the method-level editor. open a java file with many methods, select a method in the outline, then hold down up & down arrows to scroll around to other methods. the speed seems to vary, but it is generally very slow to select. as an example, on my piii 1.4 ghz with 512mb ram, it takes 10-15 seconds to scroll from the top to the bottom of the \\"workspace\\" class. this class has about 85 methods. this makes keyboard-only navigation in the content outline impractical, so this is an accessibility concern.

description: build 20020214 when moving .java files from one package to another, the move dialog is presented. the dialog has a checkbox labeled 'update references to moved elements'. this checkbox is only enabled when a valid destination package is selected. (although it does seem that there are certain cases where the ok button is enabled but the checkbox is not). i believe that this box should always be enabled: - by disabling it you enforce an unnecessary and non-obvious ordering on the user - by disabling it again after it's already been checked we give the user the impression that the elements will be renamed and there's nothing they can do about it. title: packages view shows .class and .java files when jar has source
description: if a jar is on the java build path, and the jar contains source, and the jar is the source attachment for itself, the packages view displays both the .class file and the .java file. the user can open a .class file editor, which shows the outline, or a .java file editor, which does not. this is confusing. to recreate, do the following: 1) create a java project with classes 2) export a jar file with source 3) import the jar file using the file system import 4) add the jar file to the classpath of a java project; add the jar itself as the source attachment. 5) open the java perspective and view the jar contents from the packages view. the correct behavior, since the jar is the source attachment, is to show only the .class files and filter the .java files for which the .class file exists. this scenario is not uncommon, since this is the format in which both eclipse and vaj export jars with source. in fact, some tools may want to use this format as well for custom import/export wizards.

title: inner classes should not be imported when organizing imports
description: take the following example class: package com.pcdrinc.api; public class atest { private class aninnerclass { private aninnerclass() { aninnerinnerclass obj = new aninnerinnerclass(); } private class aninnerinnerclass { private aninnerinnerclass() { } } } } after right-clicking the editor, select \\"organize imports\\" from the popup menu. the resulting file will add the line: import com.pcdrinc.api.atest.aninnerclass.aninnerinnerclass; there are two problems with this: first, inner/nested classes don't need to be imported in the file they appear in. second, this doesn't even compile since aninnerinnerclass is declared private. the \\"organize imports\\" is one of my favorite features in eclipse, but in files that have a bunch of inner classes, i always have to go up to the top and delete their imports. it would be nice if they weren't added in the first place.

title: compiler cannot resolve javax.net
description: i'm using your last stable build (20020321), and compilation fails with \\"cannot resolve javax.net\\". i'm using the latest jdk 1.4.0 from sun, and i've set all eclipse properties (that i'm aware off) to accept 1.4 features. the same source compiles using the javac compiler directly.

title: method signature list popup
description: when inside parenthesis, i can click ctrl + space to bring up a popup showing the method signature and the list of parameters and their types. a feature of this popup is that it makes the parameter that i am on into bold text and so each time there is a new ',' character, it \\"bolds\\" the next parameter. this works correctly only if i start off from the first param. in one scenario, i was trying to find the overloaded method signatures for some existing code and so pressed the ctrl + space while on the 3rd arg, but it hi-lighted the first param in the popup. i am experiencing this odd behavior in the 03/21/02 stable release.

title: adding java nature to a project does not bring it to like in package view
description: build 20020404 adding java nature is not enough to cause a project to show up inside the package view. steps: 1- create base project \\"proj\\" 2- edit its .project file to add java nature & builder: proj org.eclipse.jdt.core.javabuilder org.eclipse.jdt.core.javanature org.eclipse.team.cvs.core.cvsnature 3- switch to package view, notice that project \\"proj\\" isn't there. now go back to navigator, and force close/open of \\"proj\\". it is now listed amongst other java projects in package view.

title: open multipage editor causes invalid thread access when exporting to a jar
description: this also happens in eclipse 2.0 build 20020214 1. install the mulitpage editor example into the workspace 2. in a project create a file of type .mpe 3. a multipage editor opens on this new file. leave the editor open. 4. select file/export/jar file. fill in the jar file and click finish. you get the following jar export error: creation of jar failed invalid thread access

title: eclipse crash caused repository corruption.
description: while editing a java file pressing \\"organise imports\\" the workbench throught a java \\"outofbounds\\" error. this caused the workbench to shut down. it was not possible to restart the workbench. if the \\"lock\\" file was deleted from the matadata directory the workbench still would not restart. i was forced to create a new repository and loose all my settings.

title: mainfest file corrupt
description: hello! i have been trying to export my code, specifying a manifest, into a jar file. however, my manifest file is not placed in the jar. a blank manifest file is inserted instead. i go to file->export->jar file i select my project, mark \\"export generated class files and resources\\", specify the jar name and check the \\"compress jar\\" option. i check \\"save a description of this jar file in the workspace\\" i mark, \\"use existing manifest from the workspace\\" and specify the location of my manifest file. i couldn't attach my manifest file, but here is it's contents. . . main-class: com.sbc.cb.application class-path: . cbhelp.jar jaxb-rt-1.0-ea.jar jhall.jar lumberjack.jar pvjfc60.jar

title: new java project wizard confusing
description: - this is probably not our bug but it looks ugly: second page not properly alligned the one with the capabilities - third lets me select steps: step 1: create - creates a project step 2: add java - says: create a java project ==> do i get 2 projects? - can not go back (which i normally can in eclipse wizards) - cancel does not work (depending on when i press enter the project is created anyway but maybe without java capability

title: launch configs: junit test plugins - 'application name' unclear
description: 20020409 how are people to know which of the 2 given options they are to select? both look equally criptic

title: severe loss of context in java perspectives
description: build: 20020409 i really enjoy using the java browsing perspective but i'm really messed up everytime i want to perform a cvs operation on a class file. i known that some objects in the java views are not iresources or map to the same one, but couldn't jdt simply adapt to the container iresource? i would love to be able to select a class in the outline or class view and perform a team operation, or even see if they have outgoing changes. without this i have to switch perspectives or expand the packages

title: loading swt+examples with auto-build on causes deadlock (or takes a very long time)
description: on the 0409 build, i performed the following steps. - new workspace - enable \\"perform build automatically...\\" - connect to open source repository - select all of the following projects in the head stream: org.eclipse.swt org.eclipse.swt.examples org.eclipse.swt.examples.controls org.eclipse.swt.examples.launcher org.eclipse.swt.examples.layouts org.eclipse.swt.examples.ole.win32 org.eclipse.swt.examples.paint - do \\"check out as project\\" at this point, the progress dialog comes up indicating that the resources are being added, etc. everything proceeds normally until you get to the \\"compiling\\" step, which seems to never complete (i waited approx. 40 minutes). however, if you perform the following steps... - new workspace - disable \\"perform build automatically...\\" - connect to open source repository - select all of the following projects in the head stream: org.eclipse.swt org.eclipse.swt.examples org.eclipse.swt.examples.controls org.eclipse.swt.examples.launcher org.eclipse.swt.examples.layouts org.eclipse.swt.examples.ole.win32 org.eclipse.swt.examples.paint - do \\"check out as project\\" (does not take very long) - select project menu -> \\"rebuild all\\" ... you will see that the rebuild operation is quite quick (say, less than 1 minute) including the time to put all 7,058 errors in the task list. i believe the same amount of work ought to be happening in each case, so i suspect there may be something wrong. this is repeatable on my machine, and on another machine running win2k. my workspace was on my local c: drive.

title: decorators in packages view are "flaky"
description: 20020409 i tried to turn on the cvs decorators in the packages view by enabling window->preferences...->workbench->label decorations--cvs nothing happened. so i disabled the cvs checkbox and enabled it again and clicked apply, and i saw the decorators i wanted (i only have > and * enabled for cvs). so i clicked ok to exit the preferences dialog, and the decorators disappeared! i can repeat this fairly often, and i got vi to repeat it as well. if you disable the cvs checkbox and click apply, enable it again and click apply, and then click ok, you may or may not keep your decorators. it almost seems random. we showed the problem to someone from team, and he said it wasn't the cvs decorators misbehaving, it was decorators in general, and the fact that cvs decorators are competing/conflicting with jdt decorators when in the package view. he proved that cvs decorators were consistent in the navigator. since this is probably a generic decorator problem, this bug report is opened against ui.

title: toolbar button in ambiguous state
description: build 20020321 somehow i got the 'hide text hover' button on the toolbar into an ambiguous state. the button was displaying with a light background (as if it were depressed), but its border was not etched in. when i moved the mouse cursor over it, no 'transient' etching appeared (as if the button were disabled). the button's hover help said 'hide text hover', as if the action were active (and, indeed, text hover worked, so i assume it was active). clicking on the button had no effect. i moved my eclipse window around, and clicked around a bit, and then the button started working like a button again. sorry i don't have steps to repeat.

title: labels and widgets too far apart in preference pages
description: build: 20020411 steps: 1. click on window->preferences 2. open java->editor or java->compiler the widgets used to select options (combo boxes or color selection boxes) are right-aligned, and the labels are left aligned, leaving a large space between. this problem is magnified if the user opens a page that is wider than the default width, \\"stretching\\" the preference page dialog box. it takes more than a glance for the user to realize which labels line up with which widgets. see the ant->console page for an example of a better layout. in ant->console, the widgets are aligned, but appear closer to their labels.

title: inconsistencies for dependant options in preference pages
description: build: 20020411 steps: 1. click on window->preferences... 2. notice that the disabled label \\"number of opened editors before closing\\" lines up with the check box that enables it. 3. open the java->code generation page 4. notice that the disabled labels do not line up with the check boxes that enable them.

title: usability request: show package with hover help in hierarchy view
description: build:20020411 when browsing a hierarchy in the hierarchy view, if the user wants to find out what package a class or interface is in, the easiet way is to open it in an editor and hover over the editor tab. it would be nice if hovering over a class or interface name in the hierarchy view showed what package the class or interface was in.

title: find/replace window forgets current search string

title: search - show all occurances
description: recently a feature called \\"highlight problem\\" was added to preferences->java- >editor\\". this feature uses a gutter on the right hand side to indicate the occurances of compilation errors that are beyond user's sight (either up or down in the file) on the java editor. this feature also puts red underscores under the code to highlight the errors. this gutter is a great idea. however, it should be viewed as a common component. this is because, if a user clicks on a method name or a data member or a local variable, and requests \\"show all occurances\\", this same gutter can be used to show the search results, in a different color. the idea of underscoring errors with red is also a good one since this attracts users attention easily. along the same lines when a search is done with \\"show all occurances\\", the occurances should be underscored with a different (user configurable) color. currently the search (ctl-f) is primitive and is comparable to search in ms wordpad. with the availability of \\"show all occurances within a file\\" it would become really easy to perform one of the most common tasks that developers have at hand. this feature is very similar to \\"highlight problem\\" under preferences->java- >editor\\" and if implemented would make life so much easier. other ides have similar features and are boastful of them. thanks, vinay

title: add bookmark action is disabled in the editor
description: the add bookmark action is provided in the edit menu but it is disabled on text selections. text editors should retarget this action so that it also operates on text selections.

title: inconsistent dnd behaviour within .jar files [dnd]
description: dnd appears to be disabled from the packages view for files within a .jar file. the behaviour seems to differ based on the file extension, and will confuse the user. .class files appear to have dnd completely disabled. clicking and dragging on a .class file does not change the cursor or selection. all other file types (.html, .properties, and .mf tested) change the cursor and selection when dragged, but do not actually perform any action when dropped.

title: .class editor loss of context
description: open any .class file within a jar (with attached source) in the class editor. i used antsupport.jar from the org.eclipse.ant.core plugin. click on any method in the outline view, such that the editor scrolls down. select any other file in the packages view, and then re-select the original .class file. the editor resets the visible area to the top of the file, causing the user to lose the area where they were working.

title: refresh local in packages view
description: is it possible to add a refresh function in the context menu of an opened project in the packages view. i believe it was there some builds ago but i don't see it anymore in the m5 build. it should do the same as the refresh project in the navigator view.

title: close project should be active for packages view selections
description: build 20020501 select a project in the packages view note the top level menu item project->close project is greyed out. the action should be enabled for selections that are iadaptable and respond to the iresource.class adapter.

title: externalize strings dialog missing mnemonics
description: the externalize strings dialog needs mnemonics for strings to externalize and context

title: problems in single-click mode when open transfers focus
description: build 20020508 if a user opens a java file from the package explorer part jdt transfers focus to the newly opened editor. this causes problems if the user clicks on an element in the \\"not-focued\\" packages view since this automatically transfers focus back to the opened editor. a solution would be to not transfer focus in single click mode but i am not sure if this is what a user expects. especially since clicking on a file that opens in an external editor transfers focus to the external editor.

title: [spell checking] spell check for java comments
description: it would be really awesome to be able to have a simple spell checker for the javadoc comments. ss experience shows that some of programmers who have english as second language might benefit from such feature tremendously.

title: export to zip doesn't pick up packages view selection
description: build: 20020508 if the user selects a group of resources in the packages view, then selects file->export (and chooses to export to a zip file), when the export to zip dialog opens, no resources are selected.

title: paint listener result invisible
description: the javaeditor registers a paintlistener for error indication on it styledtextwidget. the following happens on 20020508. 1) open a java file in the java editor 2) introduce a temporary problem -> error indication is visible 3) scroll up so that the error indication is scrolled out of the visible area 4) scroll back -> error indication visible 5) scroll down so that the error indication is scrolled out of the visible area 6) scroll back -> error indication is gone note: the registered paint listener is called in both cases and also draws in both cases.

title: compile problems importing all plug-ins
description: build 20020514 fresh workspace. import all plug-ins from the runtime eclipse. compile problems show up in all ui plug-ins that have fragments. the solution is to delete all these plug-ins and import one at a time. plug-ins first followed by the fragments.

title: should have link for java perspective in welcome page
description: build 20020508 in the welcome page, the following should have a link: window > open perspective > java this didn't make sense in 1.0 since it opened a new page, hiding the welcome page. since we now share editors across perspectives, we should provide a link here. in order to do this, we need an openjavaperspective action in jdt ui which we can refer to from the welcome.xml. please let me know when this has been added so i can update the welcome.xml.

title: deleted working sets aren't removed from menu
description: build: 20020508 i created 2 new working sets, one named external tools, which consisted of the org.eclipse.ui.externaltools project. i deleted it and added a new working set, named external tools, which consosted of the same project. afterwards, both working sets named external tools appeared on the search->references menu.

title: execution arguments gets lost if starting a class file of a jar library
description: hi, i found the following bug: if you want to start a class file in a jar library, you can assign execution arguments to it, like for a normal java file you are programming. thats fine. but on the contrary of running a normal java file, execution parameter get lost, if you want to start it later again, just picking it from the \\"run\\" drop down list (or if you do a \\"relaunch last\\" (f9)). it only works, if you highligt the class in package view and click run. br, christoph.

title: source jar viewing problem
description: there is a problem with viewing source jars. it seems it is unable to recognize the source jar file (containing the source code) until the archive path is replaced and refreshed. how to reproduce the problem: 1. switch to packages view (java perspective) 2. expand a java project 3. expand a dependent jar 4. expand a package in that jar 5. double-click on any .class file in the java package result: the file .class will open a blank window (i.e. no source code can be seen) how to workaround the problem: 1. right-click the jar 2. select properties 3. select java source attachment 4. in archive field, change that to something else 5. click apply 6. then change the archive field back to the original source jar 7. click apply, then ok 8. repeat the same procedures to bring up the same .class file note: the rootpath field is empty - we do not have any prefix in the source jar result: you should now be able to see the source code for the file. (as well as for all other classes in the jar)

title: tooltips (for jdt compiler errors) stop working after switching tasks in win2k
description: i am guessing this is a general swt or swt/os interaction bug, but i have only noticed it in the jdt, so it may be specific to that plug-in. background: java compiler errors are displayed in the tasks view; as underlined code in the editor view; and (of interest here) as a circled red 'x' (or yellow lightbulb over 'x') icon in the left (breakpoint) margin of the editor view. problem: mousing over the icon should bring up a tooltip with the same text as in the tasks entry for the error, but this only works some of the time and/or stops working in the editor for no good reason. steps to reproduce: 1. open a compilable java class file. 2. add a typo (for example, an extraneous character in a class name). 3. save. 4. roll over icon to left of line with typo. tooltip describing compiler error (s) on that line should appear. 5. switch to another process in windows (click on the taskbar, for example). 6. switch back to the eclipse window. 7. roll over icon again. tooltip does not appear. at this point, no more tooltips will show up in that editor no matter what i do. if i close the editor and reopen it, tooltips will work again until i switch processes again. this is eclipse sdk 20020610.

title: refactoring alogrithm problem

title: tvt2: word order of the title needs to be changed
description: the following description is from a japanese tester working on build f2. she has tried looking for the string where \\"externalize strings in \\" would be built and has been unable to find it, as have i. her problem is that in japanese the title needs to read in a different order than it does. unless she can change the order, it just won't make sense in japanese. could we either be told where to find the proper key to switch the order, or have one made if it doesn't exist? i will also attach a screencap. this bug opened in response to tprs id=112 from the java perspective, expand the com.ibm.wsweducation.dialogs package to expose dialogsplugin.java in the packages view. double-click dialogsplugin.java to edit it if it is not already open for editing. make another change, but do not save the file. in the packages view, select the com.ibm.wsweducation.dialogs project or package. on the menu bar, click on source -> find strings to externalize... select the dialogsplugin.java file and click on externalize... then click on ok. 'externalize strings' opens. title of this window is 'externalize strings in 'dialogsplugin.java'. i found 'in' in nlsuimessage.properties file, but even if i translate it, word order is incorrect for japanese. in this case, order should be: 'dialogsplugin.jave' 'in' 'externalize strings' in japanese. we need complete sentence with variables.

title: code assist activates help ui
description: build 20020618 - launch eclipse using java.exe, and -debug with options set to show startup time - open a .java file - notice that org.eclipse.help.ui is not yet activated - do a code assist - org.eclipse.help.ui gets activated this got introduced with the fix for bug 19445, since in order to check ihelp.iscontexthelpdisplayed(), it needs to call workbenchhelp.gethelpsupport (), but this activates the help ui. the fix is to add a new api to workbenchhelp: /** * returns true if the context-sensitive help * window is currently being displayed, false if not. * this avoid activating the help support if it is not already activated. */ public static boolean iscontexthelpdisplayed() { return helpsupport != null && helpsupport.iscontexthelpdisplayed(); } and then change all senders of ihelp.iscontexthelpdisplayed() to use this instead. there are currently two: org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.classfileeditor.createjavasourceviewer (composite, iverticalruler, int) org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.compilationuniteditor.adaptedsourceviewe r.requestwidgettoken(iwidgettokenkeeper)

title: [content assist] ctrl-space offers too many options for a class with a decent size hierarchy and functionality [editor]
description: while the codeassist ctrl-space feature on a class is a wonderful feature, i often find myself with a listbox containing > 100 items. the reason for this is the presentation of the class' direct methods in addition to the methods of all classes that exist in its hierarchy going all the way back to java.lang.object. this can be easily be reproduced if you activate codeassist on any class that extends jcomponent. an alternative would be to present only the methods that are available on the class in question. the result would be a listing with a lot less noise and more applicability. since this is a significant departure from the existing functionality, i would like to request that this feature be implemented and tied to a separate keystroke (maybe ctrl-shift-space) so that developers can take the advantage of the best of both options available.

title: ability to drill down implementers' methods [type hierarchy]

description: when i call generate get/set methods or other commands which insert source code in my file, this source code is usually inserted at the bottom of the file. not the best for me. wouldn't it be possible to insert those things before all the fields in the end of the file? thomas

title: recurency between projects
description: when two project refenrence in build path to each other, there is no way to get it work. i get an message, of detected cycle in classpath. is there any way around?

title: no code assist & no getter/setter generator
description: on w xp this two features doesn't work at all: 1. code assist - i've fallowed the indications from help step by step without any results. i changed the settings for 4-5 times and tried again but it simply don't works. 2. generate getter/setter ... - a dialog box apears : (something like) \\"please select a variable or a type\\". on w 2000 the same build works ok.

title: [dialogs] bogus progress bar after canceling paste
description: build 20021016 1) select a file in the resource navigator 2) right click and choose copy 3) right click again and choose paste -> a dialog comes up asking for a new file name 4) click cancel on this dialog. -> a progress bar appears in the status line. the message says, \\"performing changes\\". the progress bar fills up immediately and then stays visible indefinitely. it only disappears when you start a new operation (such as a build).

title: autofix for unimplemented methods does not use argument names from declaration [quick fix]
description: build 20021018 - in self hosting workspace, - ensure swt has source - create a new subclass of org.eclipse.swt.widgets.layout called testlayout - notice that the two methods (computesize and layout) have argument names from the declaration, like: protected void layout(composite composite, boolean flushcache) - delete method layout - a yellow light appears on the class decl for testlayout - click on it and choose add unimplemented methods - it shows up as: protected void layout(composite arg0, boolean arg1)

title: can't have different case package names
description: if two packages have identical names but different case then eclipse complains about the project being inconsistent. i'd recommend just displaying a better error message since you can't actually have this work in windows anyway... make a new project with two source folders, create a package named \\"a\\" in one folder and a package named \\"a\\" in another folder. just for the record i wasn't the one to name the packages... michael

title: [preferences] javadoc url does not persist after eclipse is shutdown [javadoc]
description: if i go to windows -> preferences -> java -> installed jres -> select the jre that i wish to edit -> click on the edit button and put a valid javadoc url into the 'javadoc url' textfield and close the preferences, then i am able to work with them as desired. however, as soon as i close down and re-open eclipse the javadoc url string is not saved.

title: junit: would like the ability to specify test workspace location
description: i am testing pde.junit 2.1. the test workspace is always created in temp space. i would like the ability to pre-initialize a workspace and then point junit at it. when i try to run with -data the argument seems to get ignored. setting the working location does not seem to have any impact on the choice of workspace either.

title: [working sets] work space includes unselected children packages
description: if a parent package is included in a working set, child packages are automatically included even if they are explicitly un-selected. e.g. a working set is created. in it i have selected com.foo to be a member, but i did not select child package com.foo.bar. when i use the working set to filter against tasks. tasks related to com.foo.bar appear even thought they are explicitly not selected in the working set. p.s. searching the bug data base it appears there used to be a working set component, but i couldn't find it posting this bug. hopefully it will get to the correct place. thanks, john groppe

title: add javadoc comment indents too far on inner types
description: build: 200210221641 the add javadoc comment action on a type (from the outliner) creates the type template indented too far. for example: /** * */ private static class pluginhandler extends defaulthandler { note: i have modified my typecomment template to be /** * */

title: close project in package explorer
description: once upon a time it was possible to close projects from the package explorer. now this is only possible from within the navigator. is there a reason this has removed. i understand that it is not 'allowed' to open unopened projects from within the package explorer, since there is no reference to such projects, but is that the reason to also remove the close project (to maintain symmetrics.. only allow close when open is also possible), or is there another reason? anyway, i'd like it to be restored again.

title: javaeditortexthover extension-point changed
description: build 20021105 there is a new optional attribute called 'label': * label - the translatable label for this hover.

title: eclipse testrunner doesn't recognize inner test classes
description: eclipse should recognize junit tests that are inner classes, like jbuilder does. -there are many advantages to using inner classes for junit tests, such as having access to the private members of the class it's testing.

title: attach javadoc located in archive
description: when attaching javadoc to a library, the user should be able to specify a jar/zip , along with the root (like attaching source).

title: error doing java search
description: build 20021105 start search by clicking search tool bar item. java search search string = \\"imenucreator\\", case sensitive = no, search for = type, limit to = implementors, scope = workspace. search. i get the following somewhat useless message: \\"an error occurred during the search operation. 255\\" note that if i specify case sensitive = yes, i do not get the error. also, if i select imenucreator in a cu and execute search-->implementors via the context menu, i do not get the error.

title: after adding a parent folder, no longer able to add sub folder to classpath.
description: under project, run, then classpath tab. from the userclasses subtab, unselect use default class path and click advanced. use the add folders radiobox and select a folder that has subfolders. now add another except this time try to add a sub folder of the folder you just added. the folder you just added no longer appears in this list making this impossible. workaround is to first add the sub folder then add the parent folder.

title: when lightbulb suggestion appears, and is clicked on all code outside of method is cleared.

title: [dialogs] error dialog looks bad if status message is null
description: i20021127 sometime the error dialogs (org.eclipse.jface.dialogs.errordialog) show up like reason: null this is because the error dialog adds the message contained in the status without checking for null. i suggest to test for null and if it is null and the status has an exception then use status.getexception().tostring(); i agree that seeing an exception class name e.g. charencodingexception is bad - but i prefer it a 100 times over seeing null (or nothing except \\"error\\") in the ui.

title: file-wide quick fix
description: i have unit test code (and regular code) that looks like \\"this.assert...\\" and \\"this.fail...\\" which i get non-static access to static warnings. since all of our code in written in this style, we get a lot of warnings. i would like to swicth to \\"assert.assert...\\" and \\"assert.fail...\\", which eclipse now lets me do with a quick fix \\"change to declaring type\\" (as opposed to \\"change to instance type\\"), very nice! what i would like is to be able to apply a given quick fix for all of the same warnings in a file such that all of my \\"this.assert...\\" be changed to \\"assert.assert...\\". perhaps, the quick fixes pop up could be grouped in two: the single shot and file-wide ops, for example: change access to 'assert' (declaring type) change access to 'myjunittestcaseclass' (instance type) -- change all accesses to 'assert' (declaring type) change all accesses to 'myjunittestcaseclass' (instance type) ... or something like that. if eclipse has a replace feature in the search dialog i could do an re search and replace, which would not be as safe, but since this feature does not exist, i cannot and will not do it and suggest it as a workaround. futhermore, i do not particularly like to shoot myself in the foot with substitutions in res, grep or otherwise. knowing eclipse, if the feature were to be implemened, it would probably let me look at the changes before proceeding in the same manner that refactoring offers this when renaming classes, methods, etc. thank you for considering this request.

description: the tree view on the left of the 'run...' screen gets cut in half (not exactally half) each time the screen is opened. after resizing, applying other changes, choosing close then reopening the tree view is cut in half again. there is an easy workaround, just resize the two relative panes. this is happening on win2k as well as osx. although the osx problem only happens the first time you open the run panel. after you resize it once it stays the correct size.

title: change the jar export wizard to create ant build.xml
description: just a suggestion: it isn't immediately obvious to me why there needs to be a .jardesc file format, when it seems to me that ant will do all and more. the immedidate advantage for me with ant build.xml files is that they can be configured to build a jar file out of all the .class files in the project. jardesc files need to be updated every time i add or remove .java files from the project. perhaps this is possible with .jardesc files, but it isn't immediately obvious. my solution: dump .jardesc and only learn ant build.xml files.

title: [contributions] context menu contributions should support visibility element
description: m4 (i thought there was an existing pr for this issue, but i could not find it). in the java editor, the context menu contains items that only make sense when the debugger is active, e.g. inspect, display, run to line, step into selection. we should allow all context menu contributions to have a element. this is currently supported for elements, but not elements. this would allow jdt debug to set a system property when the debugger is active, and use the current support for system properties in elements to hide these actions until the debugger is active.

title: regular expression pattern in exclusion filter is too greedy in m4

title: inconsistent output when using comparrisson operators
description: i am using the jvm which is distributed with ibm wsdk 5 (the web services development kit) with eclipse 2.1. the following code produces inconsistent results in eclipse whether done from a scrapbook page or a normal class with a min method. int y = 5; int x = 2; if ( ( (x>3) && (y==5) ) | true) { system.out.print(\\"true\\"); } else { system.out.print(\\"false\\"); } the expected result is \\"true\\" as the | operator is true when either of its operands are true. the output though is nothing. i.e. it breaks the if else. single stepping shows that after evaluation, the entire if/else body is skipped. the scrap book page fails to terminate the execution thread, though the class doesn't suffer from the same problem. the workaround is simple - use the single & operator as the problem seems to be with the short-circuit operator && when the first operand evaluates to false. compiling and running against the same jvm from the command line produces the correct behaviour. i have tested with other jvm's (sun's 1.4 and websphere application server's 5.0.1) from the commmand line and these too succeed, but running from eclipse against these jvm's produces the same output of nothing. regards bruce

title: search finds only "inexact" matches
description: a project in my workspace was behaving in the way described in the following bug report: (https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=30530) that is, although the project was completely compiled and free of errors and warnings, when finding references to a method only \\"inexact\\" matches were found. for example, given two methods: public void foo(string arg) { bar(arg); } public void bar(string arg) { ... } when searching on references to bar(string), the result would be a list of \\"inexact\\" matches that matched on the method name with one argument, regardless of the parameter type. what i found out: after much hair pulling i discovered that i had a corrupt .jar file in my class path. that was the culprit. even thought that .jar was corrupt and there was no reference to it in the code, (since the project compiled correctly), it caused this strange search behavior. what i would have expected: i would expect that if i had a corrupt .jar on my class path that either: a. i would be notified about the bad .jar in the form of an error, or b. if the .jar was not referenced (thus causing no other compile errors) that the search code would ignore the .jar and work correctly. cheers to y'all at (oti)bm

title: jardesc does not allow workspace-relative paths [jar creation]
description: all path specifications in a jardesc require absolute paths. this causes problems such as this scenario: when we use cvs team integration, and we have different branches of the code line, we cannot use the same sandbox workspace folder name. so for the trunk it might be called 'myworkspace_trunk' but on the new version branch it might be called 'myworkspace_v2-1_branch'. therefore a revision managed jardesc would have to be edited on each branch code line to use the folder name of the branch as part of the absolute path. a workspace-relative path could remove the need to specify the absolute path to the output jar, and internally resolve the absolute path of the workspace such that if i say staging/myproject.jar, the logic would be relative to the specific workspace directory. it might be a nice addition to support eclipse variables as well in the path, like ${was_home}/lib/myproject.jar

title: autobuild does not kick in when using classpath containers
description: one way pde provides a sharable, dynamically adaptive classpath for plug-in projects is through the use of classpath containers. as people check out projects from cvs, import external plug-ins, delete projects, etc., the classpath of a workspace project is dynamically computed and hence always up- to-date. however, after the introduction of background autobuilding, even though the classpath does dynamically change, autobuild does not kick in. my conjecture (i love this word :-) is that autobuild does not kick in because the .classpath file does not change. ironically, the fact that the .classpath file does not change is one of the attractive aspects of classpath containers. doing the dynamic update in an iworkspacerunnable() does not help invoke autobuild in this scenario. a hack (which will be in wednesday's i-build), as suggested by one john arthorne, is to do a project.touch(monitor) on the projects for which we are updating the classpath, fooling autobuild into thinking that resources have changed. this certainly seems to work.

title: changes to class path containers should not change .project
description: this is a fork of bug 45767. the problem is this: when a classpath container changes its value, the .project file is modified. since classpaths are now dynamic but project references are not, this means end users constantly have outgoing changes on their .project files. example (from pde): - plugin b requires plugin a - plugin b is being developed in a workspace, compiling against plugin a as external jars observe: .classpath has the pde container, .project has no project references - user decides to checkout plugin a from repository to hack it observe: .project now has a new project reference. since different users on a team will have different self-hosting styles, they now have incompatible .project files.

title: the immutable bit is copied from the original resource to the ouput directory
description: eclipse version: 3.0m5 this behaviour is introduced by the fix of bug #41056. when a resource file is locked (i.e., the immutable bit is set) in the source folder, then the immutable bit is also set in te output folder. so, a rebuild of the project fails, since it can't clean the output folder. if you use the perforce scm, then all files that are not open for edit, have the immutable bit set, so all non *.java resources in the source directory that are not 'open for edit' have this problem. commenting line 157 of the file plugins/org.eclipse.core.resources.macosx/src/core.c (source distribution of m5) solves the problem. (maybe a more general solution is to make always all files in the output folder not readonly)

title: task tags starting with todo don't correctly display their priority in tasks view
description: task tags defined in preferences -> java -> task tags that are strings starting with todo and assigned other than normal priority will not have their priorities correctly displayed in the 3rd. task view column. to reproduce: 1) define a task tag in preferences -> java -> task tags for the string todo_high and assign it high priority. 2) define an additional task tag similar to step #1 for the string myhightag and also assign it high priority. 3) add 2 comment lines to a java source file, one starting with the todo_high tag and the other starting with the myhightag. 4) note in tasks view that the high priority icon is displayed for the myhightag task and no icon (indicating normal) priority is displayed for the todo_high.

title: rename "alternate jre" to "separate jre"
description: the setting on the ant jre tab for \\"alternate jre\\" actually has more meaning than just \\"alternate\\". the most important thing about this setting for ant is that it causes ant to be run in a separate vm instead of the eclipse vm. we should change the label accordingly.

title: [search] ieditormatchadapter#computecontainedmatches() and empty arrays
description: please have a look at how empty results of abstracttextsearchresult#findcontainedmatches(.) and overriding methods are handled. - the only caller, annotationmanager#addannotations(.) *can* deal with null. either it should throw an npe, or abstracttextsearchresult#findcontainedmatches(.) should explicitly allow null as result. - in javasearchresult, the method sometimes returns null - others cook their own soup with a private (sometimes static) empty_arr. if that's the approach, then abstracttextsearchresult should probably have a protected static final match[0] no_matches;.

title: dynamic project references not maintained
description: i20040428 new workspace/autobuild off 1. create a plugin project a 2. create a plugin project b 3. go to preferences -> build order. you will see a before b (either order is possible - you must edit b's plugin.xml if b is before a) 4. go to a's plugin.xml 5. add a dependency on b. (make sure you save the file) 6. go to preferences -> build order you will see a before b (still). b should now be prior to a. on build you will get an error on a: the project cannot be built until its prerequisite b is rebuilt... this error should not occur; the build order should be b then a. bug 57181 depends on this one.

title: importing preferences overwrites existing classpath variable values
description: if you export your eclipse preferences on one workstation and then import them on another, any pre-existing classpath variable values on the second workstation will be overwritten with the newly-imported values. this includes reserved variables such as jre_lib, which cannot be subsequently corrected by the user (hence the major severity of this bug). i think the way this should work is that variables which already exist on the importing workstation should not be overwritten. variables which don't already exist may be created, which will give the user a cue that s/he can subsequently alter them (their values will probably be different between workstations). at the very least, the import should ask what to do, but never overwrite reserved variables.

title: eliminating java_swt on mac os x
description: with the final version of java 1.4.2 it has become possible to launch the java vm in the first thread. this is a requirement when running an swt event loop on mac os x. until eclipse 3.0 we were using \\"java_swt\\" to launch the java vm in the first thread. in order to eliminate java_swt we need to address the following issues (in that order): swt: - java_swt calls cpsenableforegroundoperation in order to make swt applications responsive to mouse clicks. this call must be moved into the initialization code in display.java (see attachement). - if a java vm is launched directly from a command line or from an application bundle, it correctly sets the application name and icon in the dock. however, if it is launched from another process (\\"eclipse.exe\\") name and icon default to a generic name (\\"java\\") and icon. i've fixed that in java_swt by explicitely setting an icon and a name on the corresponding dock item. when eliminating java_swt this code must be moved into the initialization code in display.java as well (see attachement). (one potential obstacle here is that display.java doesn't have easy access to the eclipse icon (\\"eclips.icns\\") that lives in the application bundle and that the format of that icon isn't something swt understands). - in the info.plist file of eclipse launcher the \\"-vm\\" argument: -vm $app_package/contents/macos/java_swt can be deleted if we add the following vm argument: -xstartonfirstthread jdt: - we can remove the code from the jdt.launching that replaces calls to /usr/bin/java with \\"java_swt\\". - the mac application exporter no longer needs special support (and ui) for swt. update swt readme: - launching swt apps from the command line with /usr/bin/java is now possible if the flag -xstartonfirstthread is specified. - strangly enough application bundles just work without any additional flags after the \\"java_swt\\" has been replaced by a \\"javaapplicationstub\\" swt: - we can remove java_swt both from the platform.launcher and the binary from the swt carbon fragment.

title: [prefs] no re-compile when loading settings
description: build i0928 - user1 creates project a (no shared compiler settings) - user1 releases a to repo - user2 loads a from repo - everything in sync - user1 sets per-project compiler settings on a - user1 releases /.settings/jdt.core file to repo - user2 loads new file expected results: - compiler would use new per-project settings - build will happen to take advantage of new settings actual results: - the properties page for a shows that it is now using per-project settings - the project isn't automatically re-compiled so the new settings don't take effect not sure what the problem is here...there is probably a missing notification or something similar.

title: [call hierarchy] should allow searches for fields
description: see bug 73270 for detailed explanation. searching for references to a field, and then continuing to search for references to those references is common. the call hierarchy view allows this type of local recursive search.

title: [build path] classpath configuration only allows .jar and .zip!
description: classpath config menues only allow *.jar and *.zip. they should be editable and allow *.sar for example. workaround is strangely to type *.sar in the text-box which contains usually the selection. then also the sar files become visible.

title: [javadoc] wrongly reports invalid link format in @see and @link
description: there is nothing wrong with the sample class comment (javadoc generates the correct html without any warning or error): /** * subclasses perform gui-related work in a dedicated thread. for instructions * on using this class, see * {@link swing tutorial } * * @see * edu.oswego.cs.dl.util.concurrent * @see * jdk 5.0 * @author {@link doug lea } * @author {@link jürgen failenschmid } */ eclipse flags each line containing a href either with \\"javadoc: invalid url link format\\" or \\"javadoc: invalid reference\\".

title: package rename, "update textual matches in comments and strings" fails
description: we have the a.package1 package a.package1.class1 class containing the following comment: /*#a.package1.class2 foo*/ package1 package. now we rename the \\"package1\\" package to \\"b\\" and enable the \\"update textual matches...\\" option. the refactoring wizard preview page offers the following change for the comment aforementioned: /*#a.b.class2 foo*/ which is wrong, because not the a.package1 package is renamed. the package name substring context has to be checked in order to avoid such bad guesses.

title: generate getters and setters problem with final static variables [code manipulation]
description: when you have a final static variable in a class, the \\"generate getters and setters...\\" option will have checkboxes for creating getters and setters for this variable even though creating a setter for a final static variable doesn't really make sense. for example: public class foo { private static final string bar; } if i right click and click \\"generate getters and setters...\\", the dialogue that pops up includes a box for generating a setter for the variable bar. if that setter were created, the code will not compile. there is a dialogue warning you about creating the setter after you select it but i think it doesnt make sense to even have the option.

title: refactoring of the class name works bad for "run favorites"
description: steps to reproduce: - create hello world file. - run it by clicking on drop down arrow to the right of the run button and selecting \\"run as../java application\\" note: application is run correctly and we can see \\"hello world\\" in the console view - in the editor window select the class name click \\"ctrl+shift+r\\" and rename the class to hellowold2 - click on the run button, you will see error box \\"could not find the main class. program will exit\\". and in the console view you will see \\"java.lang.noclassdeffounderror: /hellowold2\\". note: the same goes for debug. the problem is in bad refactoring of the class name in the run/debug favorites. somehow \\".\\" (dot) is added in front of the class name. i'm using eclipse version: 3.0.0 build id: 200406251208

title: error deleting project with jar file referenced by other project
description: this problem was found using eclipse 2.1.3 but also exists in 3.0. this problem doesn't occur all the time, but below i will provide a way to reproduce this problem fairly consistently. i will also provide a fix (one line). problem: i have java project \\"x\\" which contains a jar file (my jar file is named log4j.jar). i have another java project \\"y\\" which has x's jar file on its build path. occassionally, when i try to delete x (specifying to \\"delete contents...\\"), i will get a \\"delete problems\\" dialog that reads: title: problems encountered while deleting resources. details: could not delete: /x. could not delete: d:\\dev\\workspace\\x\\log4j.jar if this error occurs i usually have to close/re-open my workspace in order to delete the project. how to reproduce: i come across this problem in more likely scenarios, but to reproduce this problem fairly consistently i just double click on the jar file (in y) to expand it and then quickly double click various packages to expand/collapse them and double click various class files to open editors, then close them, build the project, right click the project and go to the properties page - go to the \\"libraries\\" tab of the java build path page and click ok (mix up these steps - open some editors, build, close editors, etc.). doing this for less than a minute should get you in a state to reproduce the problem. for a more exact approach, you can track the number of times a java.util.zip.zipfile object is created (with your jar file as the file parameter in the constructor) vs. the number of times zipfile.close() is called (again, on a zip file representing your jar file) and wait for the number of creations to get well ahead (>5) of the number of times it is closed before you try to delete the project. if needed i can detail a fairly easy way to do this by modifying your rt.jar and replacing system.out with a custom printstream class. cause: zipfile.close() isn't being called explicitly - it appears that we're allowing garbage collection to take care of this. when we get to org.eclipse.ui.actions.deleteresourceaction.delete(iresource[], iprogressmonitor) (after following the steps above and trying to delete the project in question) - garbage collection hasn't cleaned up these unreferenced zipfile objects. proposed fix: making \\"system.gc();\\" the first line of the method: org.eclipse.ui.actions.deleteresourceaction.delete(iresource[], iprogressmonitor) fixes this problem.

title: [model] itype.resolvetype(string typename) fails
description: create a class \\"package1\\" in the \\"package1\\" package (that is, the class and its package have the same name). create classes \\"class1\\" and \\"class2\\" in the \\"package1\\" package. then let's pretend we have an itype class1 = ... corresponding to the \\"class1\\" class. now let's invoke class1.resolvetype(\\"package1.class2\\"); it returns null, presumably due to trying to resolve an inner type of the \\"package1\\" class alone, not regarding the \\"package1\\" package types. this is the same bug as the 45434, the one closed because of the lack of info. if some extra info is needed here, it will surely be supplied.

title: [api] drop to frame not enabled

title: [workingsets] problem with java workingsets
description: hi, i found following problem with workingsets from the eclipse version 3.1m5a: 1. open java perspective 2. select package explorer view 3. create new java workingset and assign java files from two projects to this workingset. 4. close one of the projects. 5. the workingset stay selected. 6. close eclipse. 7. start eclipse. 8. now all files from the closed project will be removed from the created workingset. under 3.1m3 works fine. the files from the closed project stay in the workingset.

title: [dialogs] dialogs open on wrong monitor
description: for the details see bug 58936. package explorer - new project is caused by newprojectaction which uses the shell from the workbench window - properties dialog is caused by propertydialogaction which takes a shell in the constructor.

title: [drag and drop] drag and drop (move) for project
description: drag and drop (move) for project onto explorer deletes the project from the file system. but this is not reflected in the workspace. pressing refresh - provides dialog \\"location deleted\\" and remove project from the workspace.

title: java editor cannot resolve classes named different than the filename
description: if a java file contains classes beside the class that is named like the file name and these classes are not subclasses of this \\"main\\" class and the java file has not been opened in the editor the editor cannot resolve these classes. although the project compiles successfully. example: a file test.java contains two classes: class test {} class test2 {} another file main.java in the same package contains following: public class main { test2 test2 = new test2(); } the editor marks a reference to test2 from main as error with the error message \\"test2 cannot be resolved to a type\\" if and only if the file test.java is not opened. nevertheless the project compiles successfully.

title: [formatting] 'new line after @param tags' not working
description: after uncheck the \\"new line after @param tags\\", the preview pane shows the correct format, but it doesn't work properly in the editor. it works the first time if i \\"generate getters and setters...\\", but the subsequent \\"format\\" actions will break the line into 2. the path to reproduce : project => properties => java code style => formatter => (enable project specific settings, new...) => edit... => comments i'm using versoin 3.1.0, build id: 200412162000 thanks, nathan

title: conditions do not work for jsp breakpoints
description: if you set a jsp breakpoint with the condition \\"true == false\\", it is still hit. the reason seems to be that in javalinebreakpoint.handleconditionalbreakpointevent(), the call to getjavaproject returns null. this seems to be the case because javamodelmanager.create(ifile, ijavaproject) assumes that the file is a java file, a class file or an archive file. since this is a jsp file that is passed through, it returns null rather than the correct source element.

title: enhancement persist javadoc location info to the .classpath file [buildpath]
description: assigning the javadoc information to a jar (right click properties) stores the information in the metadata repository and not to the .classpath file. hence this information is lost when moving the project to a different workspace. secondly if this information was stored in the .classpath file it could be easier to transport around. thoughts ?

title: [pull up] warn when merging constants with different initializers [refactoring]
description: situation: class b and class c both extends class a. class b and c both contain the same constant in the form 'private final static int nn = xx', but in class b the value of nn is 1, in class c the value is 2. error: in class b action refactor->pull up is called so that the constant nn is pulled up to class a. in the same action eclipse suggests to pull up the constant from class c as well. but the moved constant in class a will have the value of 1. so the constant has now a different value for class b then prior this action. conclusion: there should at least be a warning before the pull-up-action, that the two constants have different values.

title: new java project dialog too tall [code manipulation] [dialogs]
description: if i select new->project from the file menu, and then select java project (or any project for that matter) from the dialog that comes up, i get a new dialog where i can specify the project name. the dialog is called \\"new java project\\". this dialog is far too large, it doesn't fit in a 740x1024 screen even though there is plenty of empty space at the lower part of it. this means that i have to resize the dialog to be able click the buttons at the bottom of it.

title: [javadoc][format] get eclipse to integrate javadoc taglets too
description: hi, i've been supplied with some javadoc taglets, that define new tags such as @post, @pre and others. i was able to get javadoc to use them by entering the line -taglet ipsdoc.install -tagletpath \\"{path_to_my_workspace}/ipstaglets/bin\\" -link http://java.sun.com/j2se/1.4.2/docs/api in project -> generate javadoc -> next -> next -> vm options, which gives the results you can admire on http://www.student.kuleuven.ac.be/~s0165897/umlimplementation%20docs/, and i put the taglets themselves at http://www.student.kuleuven.ac.be/~s0165897/ipstaglets/. now the problem is: if i have some comments like this: /** * check whether this model element can have the given visibility as * visibility [raw]. * * @param visibility * the visibility to check. * @return false if the visibility is not effective. * | if ( visibility == null ) * | then result == false * @return true if the visibility is public. * | if ( visibility == visibility.public ) * | then result == true */ and i do autoformat (c+s+f), i get something like this: /** * check whether this model element can have the given visibility as * visibility [raw]. * @param visibility the visibility to check. * @return false if the visibility is not effective. | if ( visibility == * null ) | then result == false * @return true if the visibility is public. | if ( visibility == * visibility.public ) | then result == true */ which is of course not what i want. so what i expect is for eclipse to automatically apply the taglets and recognise the new tags. don't know whether this is possible though :-( my workaround is to disable comment formatting altogether, but that's not desirable either. cheers, h.

title: access restrictions started showing up after switching to bundle
description: here's my scenario. i have 4 plugins: 1. axis plugin, which contains no source code, only contains 3rd party jars. one of the jars is called jaxrpc.jar, which contains the javax.xml.transform.dom.domsource class file. note that this file also exists in the jdk. 2. emf-wsdl4j plugin, which has a jar called wsdl4j.jar. this jar is not exposed, ie, not part of the bundle-classpath. this jar contains a class file called javax.wsdl.wsdlexception. 3. wsdl4j plugin, which contains no source code, only contains 3rd party jars. one of the 3rd party jars is called wsdl4j.jar. this jar is exposed (part of the bundle-classpath) and again it contains a class called javax.wsdl.wsdlexception. 4. web service plugin, which depends on all the plugins above, and uses both the javax.xml.transform.dom.domsource class and the javax.wsdl.wsdlexception class. my observations: a) start with a brand new workspace b) change my target platform to one that contains all the plugins mention above c) check out the web service plugin only from cvs d) i'll get access restriction errors regarding the two classes: domsource and wsdlexception e) if i then check out the axis, emf-wsdl and wsdl plugin from cvs, then all errors go away. it looks like things start to act funny when a class is loadable from more than one location. btw, if i run my target platform standalone (not run-time workbench), things still work.

title: formatter, which would consider the manually wrapped lines

description: at the moment, its quite a hassle to create all the components necessary to utilise the events framework in an application, so i propose some ui changes to make it much easier. you should be able to create new eventlisteners and eventobjects from the wizard, and be able to refactor existing classes to allow for the handling of event listener lists, and the dispatch of events to these listeners via the appropiate methods. (addxxxlistener, removexxxlistener, notifyxxx) this would be quite a good thing to implement, because coding events do take up a lot of time, and a lot of people don't knowhow to do it properly (wizard would make it uniform and easy to do). there are probably ways we can optimise the event wizards as well. for example, you might have an overall 'create event' wizard, and you might be able to choose an appropiate dispatcher class to use from there.

title: [quick fix] no quick fixes for marker with imarker.line_number and no imarker.char_start and imarker.char_end
description: i'm creating (problem) markers for a java file and i only have a line number available when i create the marker. i add the imarker.line_number attribute to the marker attributes, but do not specify a char_start or char_end. the marker shows up in the file, but there are no quick fixes available for it (using ctrl+1 or right click on the marker). when i click on the marker in the problems view, however, i get the quick fixes that are possible. (this used to work in 3.0, doesnt now in 3.1) i traced through the code and found that the markers with a line number get their end and start range set to be the same in: abstractmarkerannotationmodel.createpositionfrommarker(imarker marker). because the start and end are both -1 coming into the method, end = start. in javacorrectionassistant.collectquickfixableannotations(), there is a check to see if the position for the offset is within the range -- its a call to javacorrectionassistant.isinside(). isinside has the following body: private static boolean isinside(int offset, int start, int end) { return offset >= start && offset < end; } but, because the start and end are set to be the same, its never inside. the net effect: any markers with a position set via line_number will not get a quick fix.

title: [static imports] missing error message: name collision due to static import.
